title.zh: 卷六十九 列傳第七: 太祖諸子 宗雋本名訛魯觀 宗傑本名沒里野 宗強本名阿魯，子:爽（本名阿鄰）可喜 阿瑣 宗敏本名阿魯補 元本名常勝
title.en: Volume 69 Biographies 7: Taizu sons - Zong Jun formerly named Eluguan, Zong Jie formerly named Meiliye, Zong Qiang formerly named Alu, son: Shuang (formerly named Alin) kexi, A Suo, Zong Min formerly named Alubu, Yuan formerly named Changsheng
title.raw: 卷六十九 列傳第七: 太祖諸子 宗雋本名訛魯觀 宗傑本名沒里野 宗強本名阿魯，子:爽（本名阿鄰）可喜 阿瑣 宗敏本名阿魯補 元本名常勝 Volume 69 Biographies 7: Taizu sons - Zong Jun formerly named Eluguan, Zong Jie formerly named Meiliye, Zong Qiang formerly named Alu, son: Shuang (formerly named Alin) kexi, A Suo, Zong Min formerly named Alubu, Yuan formerly named Changsheng

sentences.zh: 列傳第七 太祖諸子 宗雋本名訛魯觀 宗傑本名沒里野 宗強本名阿魯，子 爽

translations.literal: Biography 7: Sons of the Taizu—Zong Juan (born Eluguan), Zong Jie (born Meiliye), Zong Qiang (born Alu); his son Shuang
translations.idiomatic: Biography 7. Sons of Taizu: Zong Juan, born Eluguan; Zong Jie, born Meiliye; Zong Qiang, born Alu—and Shuang his son.

sentences.zh: （本名阿鄰）

translations.literal: (born Alin)
translations.idiomatic: (born Alin)

sentences.zh: 可喜 阿瑣 宗敏本名阿魯補 元宗峻子，本名常勝

translations.literal: Kexi, A Suo, Zong Min (born Alubu); Yuan, son of Zong Jun, born Changsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kexi, A Suo, Zong Min (born Alubu); Yuan, son of Zong Jun, born Changsheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖聖穆皇后生景宣帝、豐王烏烈、趙王宗傑。

translations.literal: The Taizu's Empress Shengmu bore the Jingxuan Emperor, Prince Feng Wulie, and Prince Zhao Zong Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shengmu, consort of Taizu, bore the Jingxuan Emperor, Prince Feng Wulie, and Prince Zhao Zong Jie.

sentences.zh: 光懿皇后生遼王宗幹。

translations.literal: Empress Guangyi bore Prince Liao Zong Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Guangyi bore Prince Liao Zong Gan.

sentences.zh: 欽憲皇后生宋王宗望、陳王宗雋、瀋王訛魯。

translations.literal: Empress Qinxian bore Prince Song Zong Wang, Prince Chen Zong Juan, and Prince Shen Elu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinxian bore Prince Song Zong Wang, Prince Chen Zong Juan, and Prince Shen Elu.

sentences.zh: 宣獻皇后生睿宗、豳王訛魯朵。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanxian bore the Ruizong and Prince Bin Eluduo.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanxian bore Ruizong and Prince Bin Eluduo.

sentences.zh: 元妃烏古論氏生梁王宗弼、衛王宗強、蜀王宗敏。

translations.literal: The primary consort, Lady Wugulun, bore Prince Liang Zong Bi, Prince Wei Zong Qiang, and Prince Shu Zong Min.
translations.idiomatic: Primary consort Lady Wugulun bore Prince Liang Zong Bi, Prince Wei Zong Qiang, and Prince Shu Zong Min.

sentences.zh: 崇妃蕭氏生紀王習泥烈、息王甯吉、莒王燕孫。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Xiao bore Prince Ji Xinilie, Prince Xi Ningji, and Prince Ju Yansun.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Xiao bore Prince Ji Xinilie, Prince Xi Ningji, and Prince Ju Yansun.

sentences.zh: 娘子獨奴可生鄴王斡忽。

translations.literal: The lady Dunuke bore Prince Ye Gahuo.
translations.idiomatic: The consort Dunuke bore Prince Ye Gahuo.

sentences.zh: 宗幹、宗望、宗弼自有傳。

translations.literal: Zong Gan, Zong Wang, and Zong Bi have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Gan, Zong Wang, and Zong Bi are treated in separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 爽，本名阿鄰。

translations.literal: Shuang, born Alin.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang—born Alin.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，授世襲猛安。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande he was granted a hereditary meng'an command.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande year 3 he received a hereditary meng'an commission.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，除橫海軍節度使，改安武軍，留京師奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he was made military commissioner of the Henghai Army, then transferred to the Anwu Army, remaining in the capital to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglong year 2: appointed military commissioner of the Henghai Army, then of the Anwu Army, and kept at the capital on court attendance.

sentences.zh: 海陵將伐宋，嚴酒禁，爽坐與其弟阿瑣，及從父兄京、徒單貞會飲，被杖，下遷歸化州刺史，奪猛安。

translations.literal: As Hailing prepared to attack Song, liquor was strictly forbidden. Shuang was punished for drinking with his brother A Suo and his clansman cousins Jing and Tushan Zhen; he was beaten, demoted to prefect of Guihua, and stripped of his meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was about to march on Song he banned wine outright. Shuang had drunk with his brother A Suo and with his cousins Jing and Tushan Zhen; he was flogged, demoted to prefect of Guihua, and lost his meng'an.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複除安武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed military commissioner of the Anwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reappointed military commissioner of the Anwu Army.

sentences.zh: 海陵渡淮，分遣使者翦滅宗室，爽憂懼不知所出。

translations.literal: When Hailing crossed the Huai, he dispatched envoys to cut down the imperial clan. Shuang was terrified and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing crossed the Huai and sent agents to purge the clan. Shuang was sick with fear and could see no way out.

sentences.zh: 會世宗即位東京，宗室璋推爽弟阿瑣行中都留守，遣人報爽。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne at Dongjing, the clansman Zhang urged A Suo, Shuang's brother, to act as temporary protector of Zhongdu and sent word to Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong came to the throne at Dongjing. The clansman Zhang had A Suo, Shuang's younger brother, hold Zhongdu as acting protector and sent to inform Shuang.

sentences.zh: 爽棄妻子來奔，與弟忻州刺史可喜，俱至中都。

translations.literal: Shuang abandoned wife and children and came over; with his brother Kexi, prefect of Xin, he reached Zhongdu together.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang left wife and children behind and fled to join him; with his brother Kexi, prefect of Xin, he entered Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 東迎車駕，至梁魚務入見，世宗大悅，即除殿前馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He went east to meet the imperial carriage, presented himself at Liangyuwu, and Shizong was greatly pleased; at once Shuang was made commander-in-chief of the palace horse and foot armies before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He rode east to meet the imperial train, was received at Liangyuwu, and Shizong rejoiced; at once Shuang was made commander of the Palace Horse and Foot Armies before the throne.

sentences.zh: 封溫王，改秘書監。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince Wen and made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Prince Wen and appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 母憂，尋起複，遷太子太保，進封壽王。

translations.literal: On mourning for his mother he was soon recalled; promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and advanced to Prince Shou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office, but was soon recalled, made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and advanced to Prince Shou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，世宗第五女蜀國公主下嫁唐括鼎，賜宴神龍殿，謂爽曰：「朕與卿兄弟，在正隆時，朝夕常懼不保，豈意今日賴爾兄弟之福，可以享安樂矣。

translations.literal: Before long, Shizong's fifth daughter, Princess of Shu, married Tangguo Ding; a banquet was given in the Shenlong Hall. The emperor said to Shuang: 「You and your brothers—in the Zhenglong years we lived in daily fear that we might not survive. Who could have thought that today, through your brothers' fortune, we might enjoy peace and ease?
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Shizong's fifth daughter, the Princess of Shu, married Tangguo Ding; a feast was held in the Shenlong Hall. The emperor said to Shuang, 「You and your brothers—in the Zhenglong years we woke each day afraid we would not live to see the next. Who dreamed that today, by your brothers' blessing, we could sit in ease?

sentences.zh: 」爽泣下，頓首謝。

translations.literal: 」Shuang wept and bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: 」Shuang wept and bowed to the ground.

sentences.zh: 未幾，判大宗正事，太子太保如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was assigned to preside over the Imperial Clan Court, retaining his title as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was put in charge of the Imperial Clan Court while keeping his rank as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 爽有疾，詔除其子符寶祗候思列為忠順軍節度副使。

translations.literal: When Shuang fell ill, an edict appointed his son, Sigil Guard Attendant Silie, deputy military commissioner of the Zhongshun Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang fell ill; an edict made his son Silie, a Sigil Guard Attendant, deputy military commissioner of the Zhongshun Army.

sentences.zh: 爽入謝，上曰：「朕以卿疾，使卿子遷官，冀卿因喜而愈也。

translations.literal: Shuang came in to give thanks. The emperor said: 「Because of your illness I have promoted your son, hoping that joy may help you recover.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang came to give thanks. The emperor said, 「Your illness moved me to advance your son—I hoped gladness might ease you.

sentences.zh: 思列年少，未閑政事，卿訓以義方，使有善可稱，別加升擢。

translations.literal: Silie is young and not yet skilled in state affairs; instruct him in proper conduct so that he may earn praise, and I shall promote him further.
translations.idiomatic: Silie is young and untried in government; teach him the right way so he may deserve praise, and I will raise him further.

sentences.zh: 」爽疾少間，將從上如涼陘，賜錢千萬，進封英王，轉太子太傅。

translations.literal: 」When Shuang's illness eased somewhat and he was to accompany the emperor to Liangxi, ten million cash were granted; he was advanced to Prince Ying and made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: 」When Shuang was somewhat better and was to follow the emperor to Liangxi, he received ten million cash, was advanced to Prince Ying, and made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 複世襲猛安，進封榮王，改太子太師。

translations.literal: His hereditary meng'an was restored; he was advanced to Prince Rong and made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His hereditary meng'an was restored; he was advanced to Prince Rong and made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 顯宗長女鄴國公主下嫁烏古論誼，賜宴慶和殿，爽坐西向，迎夕照，面發赤似醉。

translations.literal: The Xianzong's eldest daughter, Princess of Ye, married Wugulun Yi; a banquet was given in the Qinghe Hall. Shuang sat facing west, catching the evening sun; his face flushed red as though drunk.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianzong's eldest daughter, Princess of Ye, married Wugulun Yi; a feast was given in the Qinghe Hall. Shuang sat facing west into the sunset; his face burned red as if he were drunk.

sentences.zh: 上問曰：「卿醉邪？

translations.literal: The emperor asked, 「Are you drunk?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, 「Are you drunk?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「未也，臣面迎日色，非酒紅也。

translations.literal: 」He replied, 「No, Your Majesty. My face catches the sunlight—it is not wine that reddens it.
translations.idiomatic: 」He answered, 「No, sire. I am facing the sun—that flush is not from wine.

sentences.zh: 」上悅，顧群臣曰：「此弟出言，未嘗不實，自小如此。

translations.literal: 」The emperor was pleased and said to the assembled ministers, 「This younger brother of mine has never spoken falsely—he has been so since childhood.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor was pleased and told the ministers, 「This brother of mine has never told a lie—not since he was a boy.

sentences.zh: 」因謂顯宗兄弟曰：「汝等可以為法。

translations.literal: 」He then told the Xianzong and his brothers, 「You may take him as your model.
translations.idiomatic: 」Then he said to the Xianzong and his brothers, 「You would do well to be like him.

sentences.zh: 」以爽貲用有闕，特賜錢一萬貫。

translations.literal: 」Because Shuang's private means were insufficient, ten thousand strings of cash were specially granted.
translations.idiomatic: 」Learning that Shuang's household was short, the emperor specially granted ten thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，爽疾久不愈，敕有司曰：「榮王告滿百日，當給以王俸。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Shuang's illness lingered. An edict instructed the offices: 「When Prince Rong's mourning leave reaches one hundred days, he shall receive a prince's stipend.」
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 Shuang's illness would not lift. An edict ran: 「When Prince Rong's sick leave reaches one hundred days, grant him a prince's salary.」

sentences.zh: 既薨，上悼痛，輟朝，遣官致祭，賻銀千兩、重彩四十端、絹四百匹。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor grieved deeply, suspended court, sent officers to perform the sacrifices, and granted a funeral gift of one thousand taels of silver, forty bolts of heavy brocade, and four hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor mourned deeply, halted court, sent officers to sacrifice, and granted one thousand taels of silver, forty bolts of heavy brocade, and four hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 陪葬山陵，親王、百官送葬。

translations.literal: He was buried beside the imperial tombs; princes and officials escorted the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried with the imperial tombs; princes and officials followed the bier.

sentences.zh: 他日，謂大臣曰：「榮王之葬，朕以不果親送為恨。

translations.literal: On another day he said to his ministers, 「At Prince Rong's burial I regret that I could not go in person to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he told his ministers, 「At Prince Rong's funeral I could not go myself—that still grieves me.

sentences.zh: 」其見友愛如此。

translations.literal: 」Such was the affection he showed him.
translations.idiomatic: 」Such was the love he bore him.

sentences.zh: 可喜，以宗室子，累官唐括部族節度使，降忻州刺史。

translations.literal: Kexi, as a clansman, rose through offices to military commissioner of the Tangguo tribal command, then was reduced to prefect of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Kexi, of the imperial clan, rose to military commissioner of the Tangguo tribal command, then was demoted to prefect of Xin.

sentences.zh: 海陵遣使殺之，可喜聞世宗即位，即棄州來歸，與其兄歸化州刺史阿鄰會於中都。

translations.literal: Hailing sent agents to kill him. When Kexi heard that Shizong had taken the throne, he at once abandoned his prefecture and came over; he met his elder brother Alin, prefect of Guihua, at Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing sent men to kill him. Hearing that Shizong had taken the throne, Kexi abandoned his post and fled in; he met his elder brother Alin, prefect of Guihua, at Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 是時，弟阿瑣權中都留守事，可喜謂阿鄰曰：「阿瑣愚戇，恐不能撫治，欲少留以助之。

translations.literal: At that time his brother A Suo was acting as temporary protector of Zhongdu. Kexi said to Alin, 「A Suo is dull and rough; I fear he cannot govern well. I wish to remain a little while to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: A Suo was then acting protector of Zhongdu. Kexi said to Alin, 「A Suo is slow and blunt; I doubt he can hold the city. Let me stay a while to help him.

sentences.zh: 」阿鄰乃行。

translations.literal: 」Alin then departed.
translations.idiomatic: 」Alin went on.

sentences.zh: 可喜留中都，聞世宗發東京，乃迎見於麻吉鋪。

translations.literal: Kexi stayed in Zhongdu; when he heard that Shizong had set out from Dongjing, he went to meet him at Majipu.
translations.idiomatic: Kexi remained at Zhongdu; when he heard the emperor had left Dongjing, he went out to meet him at Majipu.

sentences.zh: 除兵部尚書，佩金牌，將兵往南京。

translations.literal: He was made Minister of War, given a golden tablet, and sent with troops toward Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of War, given a golden tablet, and marched toward Nanjing with troops.

sentences.zh: 行至中都，聞南京已定，遂止。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhongdu he heard that Nanjing was already secured, and halted.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongdu he learned Nanjing was already settled, and stopped.

sentences.zh: 可喜材武過人，狠戾好亂，自乙太祖孫，頗有異志。

translations.literal: Kexi was gifted in arms beyond the common run, cruel and bent on turmoil; as a grandson of Taizu in the yi generation, he harbored no small ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Kexi was fierce in battle beyond others, cruel and eager for disorder; a grandson of Taizu in the yi line, he nursed no small designs.

sentences.zh: 世宗初至中都，倥傯多事，扈從諸軍未暇行賞，或有怨言。

translations.literal: When Shizong had just reached Zhongdu, affairs pressed on every side; the armies that had escorted him had not yet been rewarded, and some murmured in complaint.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong had just entered Zhongdu, business crowded him on every side; the troops who had escorted him had not yet been rewarded, and some grumbled.

sentences.zh: 昭武大將軍斡論，正隆末，被詔佩金牌，取河南兵四百人，監完顏彀英軍於歸化，次彰德。

translations.literal: Grand General of Martial Illumination Wolun—at the end of the Zhenglong era, by edict wore the golden plaque, took four hundred Henan troops, supervised Wanyan Gu Ying's army at Guihua, and halted at Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: Wolun, Grand General of Martial Illumination, late in the Zhenglong reign was ordered to wear the golden plaque, muster four hundred troops from Henan, and oversee Wanyan Gu Ying's forces at Guihua, stopping at Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 會獨吉和尚持大定赦文至。

translations.literal: Duji Heshang arrived bearing the Dading amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Duji Heshang arrived with the amnesty proclamation of the Dading reign.

sentences.zh: 和尚使人招之，斡論不聽，率兵來迎，和尚亦以所將蒲輦兵，列陣待之。

translations.literal: Heshang sent men to summon him; Wolun would not obey, led troops to meet him; Heshang likewise arrayed his Pulan troops in battle order to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Heshang sent envoys to call him in; Wolun refused and marched to confront him. Heshang, for his part, drew up the Pulan troops he commanded and waited in battle array.

sentences.zh: 斡論兵皆不肯戰，遂請降。

translations.literal: Wolun's soldiers all refused to fight, and thereupon sought surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wolun's men would not fight at all, and so they asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 和尚邀之入相州，收其甲兵，置酒相勞，斡論托腹疾，不肯飲。

translations.literal: Heshang invited him into Xiang Prefecture, collected their armor and weapons, set out wine to reward them; Wolun pleaded belly ailment and would not drink.
translations.idiomatic: Heshang brought him into Xiang Prefecture, disarmed his men, and set a feast to honor them. Wolun claimed a stomach ailment and would not drink.

sentences.zh: 至夜，已張燈，時時出門，與其心腹密謀，欲就執和尚。

translations.literal: When night came, lamps already lit, he went out the door from time to time and with his intimates secretly plotted to seize Heshang on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: By night, with lamps already burning, he slipped out again and again to conspire with his closest followers—they meant to seize Heshang then and there.

sentences.zh: 稍具弓矢，和尚覺之，佯為不知，使其從者迫而伺之，斡論不得發。

translations.literal: They somewhat prepared bows and arrows; Heshang noticed but pretended not to know, and had his followers press close and watch; Wolun could not act.
translations.idiomatic: Bows and arrows were quietly readied. Heshang saw it but played ignorant, ordering his attendants to crowd in and watch; Wolun never found his opening.

sentences.zh: 上至中都近郊，斡論上謁，上亦撫慰之。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached the outskirts of the Central Capital, Wolun came to audience; the emperor also comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came to the suburbs of the Central Capital, Wolun presented himself; the emperor received him with reassurance.

sentences.zh: 斡論自慊，初無降志。

translations.literal: Wolun felt ashamed—in the beginning he had had no mind to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wolun was ill at ease with himself; he had never meant to submit in the first place.

sentences.zh: 及河南統軍司令史斡里朵，為人狡險，憙圖事，斡論取兵于河南統軍使陁滿訛里也，斡里朵與俱來，俱不自安。

translations.literal: Moreover the Henan frontier army commander-in-chief's clerk Wolidu was deceitful and dangerous by nature, fond of plotting; Wolun had drawn troops from the Henan frontier army commissioner Tuoman E'eli—Wolidu came along with them, and all were ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Then there was Wolidu, clerk to the Henan frontier commander—a man sly, treacherous, and greedy for intrigue. Wolun had taken soldiers from the Henan frontier commissioner Tuoman E'eli; Wolidu came with them, and none of the party felt secure.

sentences.zh: 同知延安尹李惟忠，與熙宗弑逆，構殺韓王亨，世宗疏斥之。

translations.literal: Vice Director of Yan'an Yin Li Weizhong, with the regicide against Xizong, had framed and killed Prince of Han Hen; Shizong had kept him at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Weizhong, Vice Director of Yan'an, had taken part in the plot that murdered Xizong and had engineered the death of Prince of Han Hen; Shizong had cast him aside.

sentences.zh: 同知中都留守璋，初自領其職，因而授之。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Central Capital garrison Zhang—at first he had taken the post on his own authority, and it was afterward conferred on him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Vice Director of the Central Capital garrison, had first seized the office for himself; only later was the appointment made formal.

sentences.zh: 完顏布輝為副統，以罪解職，居京師。

translations.literal: Wanyan Buhui had been deputy commander-in-chief, was dismissed from office for a crime, and dwelt in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Buhui had served as deputy commander-in-chief, lost his post for an offense, and was living in the capital.

sentences.zh: 於是可喜、斡論、李惟忠、斡里朵、璋、布輝謀，欲因扈從軍士怨望作亂。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kexi, Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Zhang, and Buhui plotted, intending to exploit the resentments of the attendant-follower soldiers and raise a revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Then Kexi, Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Zhang, and Buhui conspired to turn the grumbling of the emperor's escort troops into open rebellion.

sentences.zh: 斡論曰：「押軍猛安沃窟刺，必不違我。

translations.literal: Wolun said: 「The supervising army meng'an Wokulu will surely not oppose me.
translations.idiomatic: Wolun said: 「The escort meng'an Wokulu will never go against me.

sentences.zh: 」惟忠曰：「惟忠嘗為神翼軍總管，有兩銀牌尚在，可以矯發內藏賞士。

translations.literal: 」Li Weizhong said: 「Weizhong once served as chief of the Divine Wing Army; I still have two silver plaques, and can use them to falsely issue rewards from the inner storehouse to soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: 」Li Weizhong said: 「I was once chief of the Divine Wing Army and still hold two silver plaques—I can forge orders to pay out the inner treasury's bounty to the troops.

sentences.zh: 萬戶高松與我舊，必見聽。

translations.literal: The wanhu Gao Song is an old associate of mine—he is sure to heed me.
translations.idiomatic: The wanhu Gao Song is an old friend of mine; he is bound to listen.

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「若得此軍，舉事無難矣。

translations.literal: 」The assembly said: 「If we obtain this army, raising the affair will be no great difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: 」The others said: 「With that force in hand, the deed will not be hard.

sentences.zh: 」斡論往約沃窟刺，沃窟刺從之。

translations.literal: 」Wolun went to arrange it with Wokulu, and Wokulu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wolun went to win Wokulu over, and Wokulu consented.

sentences.zh: 惟忠旆說高松，高松不聽，語在《松傳》。

translations.literal: Li Weizhong went to persuade Gao Song; Gao Song would not listen—the account is in the Biography of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Li Weizhong went to win over Gao Song, but Gao Song refused—the story is told in the Biography of Song.

sentences.zh: 大定二年正月甲戌，上謁山陵，可喜中道稱疾而歸。

translations.literal: Dading year 2, first month, day jiaxu—the emperor visited the imperial tombs; Kexi on the way pleaded illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading, on jiaxu of the first month, the emperor went to the imperial tombs. Kexi, midway, claimed illness and turned back.

sentences.zh: 乙亥夜，召斡論、惟忠、斡里朵、璋、布輝會其家，沃窟刺以兵赴之，璋曰：「今不高松軍，事不可成矣。

translations.literal: On the night of yihai he summoned Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Zhang, and Buhui to meet at his house; Wokulu came with troops; Zhang said: 「Without Gao Song's army now, the affair cannot succeed.
translations.idiomatic: That night, on yihai, he called Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Zhang, and Buhui to his home. Wokulu came with soldiers. Zhang said: 「Without Gao Song's troops, this cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 」可喜、璋、布輝乃擒斡論、惟忠、斡里朵、沃窟刺，詣有司自首。

translations.literal: 」Kexi, Zhang, and Buhui thereupon seized Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, and Wokulu and went to the authorities to confess voluntarily.
translations.idiomatic: 」Kexi, Zhang, and Buhui then seized Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, and Wokulu and surrendered themselves to the officials.

sentences.zh: 既下詔獄，可喜不肯自言其始謀，及與斡論面質，然後款伏。

translations.literal: Once they were placed in the imperial prison, Kexi would not speak of his initial plotting on his own; only when confronted face to face with Wolun did he then confess in full.
translations.idiomatic: After they were committed to the imperial prison, Kexi would not admit the original plot of his own accord; only when he was confronted with Wolun did he confess everything.

sentences.zh: 上念兄弟少，太祖孫惟數人在，惻然傷之。

translations.literal: The emperor reflected that brothers were few and only a handful of Taizu's grandsons remained—he was moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought how few brothers he had left, and that of Taizu's grandsons only a handful still lived—his heart ached for them.

sentences.zh: 詔罪止可喜一身，其兄弟子孫皆不緣坐。

translations.literal: An edict declared guilt rested on Kexi alone; his brothers, sons, and grandsons were none implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: An edict fixed guilt on Kexi alone; brothers, sons, and grandsons would not be punished by association.

sentences.zh: 遂誅斡論、惟忠、斡里朵、沃窟刺等，其沃窟刺下謀克士卒皆釋之。

translations.literal: Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Wokulu, and the rest were then executed; the soldiers under Wokulu's subordinate company commands were all released.
translations.idiomatic: Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Wokulu, and the others were put to death; the company-command soldiers under Wokulu were all released.

sentences.zh: 除璋彰化軍節度使，布輝浚州防禦使。

translations.literal: Zhang was appointed military commissioner of Zhanghua Army; Buhui was made defender of Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was made military commissioner of Zhanghua; Buhui was made defender of Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔天下。

translations.literal: On xinsi an edict was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi an edict went out to all the realm.

sentences.zh: 是日，賜扈從萬戶銀百兩，猛安五十兩，謀克絹十匹，甲士絹五匹、錢六貫，阿里喜以下賜各有差。

translations.literal: That day, attendant-follower wanhu were granted a hundred taels of silver, meng'an fifty taels, company commanders ten bolts of silk, armored soldiers five bolts of silk and six strings of cash—those below Ali Xi received gifts in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the escort wanhu received a hundred taels of silver, meng'an fifty taels, company commanders ten bolts of silk, and armored soldiers five bolts of silk plus six strings of cash; ranks below Ali Xi were rewarded in due measure.

sentences.zh: 阿瑣，宗強之幼子也。

translations.literal: Asuo was the youngest son of Zong Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Asuo was Zong Qiang's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 長身多力。

translations.literal: He was tall of frame and possessed great strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and immensely strong.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，以宗室子，授奉國上將軍，累加金吾衛上將軍，居於中都。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande, as a member of the imperial clan he was appointed General-in-Chief Who Serves the State; he rose to General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guards and resided in the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande, as a clansman he was made General-in-Chief Who Serves the State, later promoted to General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guards, and lived at the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，授橫海軍節度使，剛以名鷹，詔曰：「卿方年少，宜自戒慎，留心政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was appointed military commissioner of the Transverse Sea Army; he was stubborn and, on account of a famous hawk, received an edict saying: 「You are still young—you should warn yourself and be cautious, and give your mind to administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he was made military commissioner of the Transverse Sea Army. He was headstrong and kept a celebrated hawk; an edict said: 「You are still young. Guard yourself, stay wary, and attend to your duties.

sentences.zh: 」改武定軍，以母憂去官。

translations.literal: 」He was transferred to Wuding Army; on his mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was moved to Wuding Army, then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 起復興平軍節度使，賜以襲衣廄馬。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning, he was made military commissioner of Xingping Army and granted court robes and stable horses.
translations.idiomatic: Called back from mourning, he was appointed military commissioner of Xingping and given court dress and horses from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 遷廣甯尹，坐贓一萬四千餘貫，詔杖八十，削兩階，解職。

translations.literal: Promoted to Director of Guangning, he was convicted of embezzling more than fourteen thousand strings; by edict he received eighty blows with the staff, was reduced two ranks, and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: As Director of Guangning he was found guilty of embezzling more than fourteen thousand strings of cash. By edict he was beaten eighty strokes, stripped of two ranks, and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 入見於常武殿，上曰：「朕謂汝有才力，使之臨民。

translations.literal: He entered audience at the Ever Martial Hall; the emperor said: 「We considered you possessed of talent and force and made you preside over the people.
translations.idiomatic: He came before the throne in the Ever Martial Hall. The emperor said: 「I thought you had ability and made you govern the people.

sentences.zh: 今汝在法當死，朕以親親之故，曲為全貸。

translations.literal: Now by the law you deserve death; we, for the sake of kinship, have bent to grant you full pardon.
translations.idiomatic: By law you should die now; for kinship's sake I bend the rule and spare you outright.

sentences.zh: 當思自今戒懼，勿複使惡聲達於朕聽。

translations.literal: You should think from this day to warn yourself in fear—do not again let evil report reach our ears.
translations.idiomatic: From this day forward, live in fear and restraint—do not let ill report of you reach my ears again.

sentences.zh: 」改平涼、濟南尹，卒官，年三十七。

translations.literal: 」He was changed to Director of Pingliang and Jinan; he died in office, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was reassigned as Director of Pingliang and Jinan, and died in office at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 上命有司致祭，賻銀千兩、重彩四十端、絹四百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the authorities to perform the offering sacrifice; funeral gifts were a thousand taels of silver, forty bolts of heavy-color silk, and four hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the officials to conduct the funeral rites and sent a thousand taels of silver, forty bolts of heavy brocade, and four hundred bolts of silk as burial gifts.

sentences.zh: 海陵謀弑立，畏宗敏尊且材勇，欲構誣以除之。

translations.literal: Hailing plotted regicide and usurpation; he feared Zong Min's eminence and martial talent and wished to fabricate charges to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing plotted murder and usurpation, he feared Zong Min—high in rank, brave and capable—and meant to frame him and destroy him.

sentences.zh: 時熙宗屢殺大臣，宗敏憂之，謂海陵曰：「主上喜殘殺，而國家事重，奈何。

translations.literal: At that time Xizong repeatedly killed great ministers; Zong Min was troubled and said to Hailing: 「Our lord delights in cruel killing, yet the affairs of state are weighty—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: In those days Xizong was slaughtering ministers one after another. Zong Min, uneasy, said to Hailing: 「The sovereign delights in bloodshed, yet the realm hangs in the balance—what can be done?

sentences.zh: 」宗敏言時，適左右無人，海陵將以此為指斥構害之，自念無證不可發，乃止。

translations.literal: 」When Zong Min spoke, there happened to be no one else present; Hailing was about to use this as an indictment of disrespect and frame him—but reflected that without evidence he could not proceed, and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: 」No one else was near when he spoke. Hailing nearly seized on the words as lese-majeste and moved to destroy him, but saw he had no proof and held back.

sentences.zh: 及弑熙宗，使葛王宗敏。

translations.literal: When he murdered Xizong, he dispatched Prince of Ge Zong Min.
translations.idiomatic: After he killed Xizong, he sent for Prince of Ge Zong Min.

sentences.zh: 葛王者，世宗初封也。

translations.literal: Prince of Ge—that was Shizong's initial enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ge was the title Shizong had first received.

sentences.zh: 宗敏聞海陵召，疑懼不敢往。

translations.literal: Zong Min, hearing Hailing's summons, was doubtful and afraid and did not dare go.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Min heard Hailing summon him, he was afraid and did not dare go.

sentences.zh: 葛王曰：「叔父今不即往，至明日，如何與之相見。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ge said: 「Uncle, if you do not go at once today, when tomorrow comes how will you face him?
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ge said: 「Uncle, if you do not go today, how will you meet him tomorrow?

sentences.zh: 」宗敏入宮，海陵欲殺之，尚猶豫，以問左右。

translations.literal: 」Zong Min entered the palace; Hailing wished to kill him but still hesitated, and questioned those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zong Min entered the palace. Hailing meant to kill him but still wavered, and asked his attendants what to do.

sentences.zh: 烏帶曰：「彼太祖子也，不殺之，眾人必有異議，不如除之。

translations.literal: Wudai said: 「He is a son of the Taizu—if he is not killed, the multitude will surely raise objections; better to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Wudai said: 「He is Taizu’s own son. Leave him alive and the court will murmur—better cut him down.

sentences.zh: 」乃使僕散忽土殺之，忽土刃擊宗敏，宗敏左右走避，膚發血肉，狼藉遍地。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon he had Pusan Hutu kill him; Hutu struck Zong Min with his blade—Zong Min’s attendants fled aside, skin, hair, flesh, and blood strewn over the ground.
translations.idiomatic: 」He sent Pusan Hutu to do it. Hutu hacked at Zong Min; his attendants scattered. Flesh and blood lay heaped across the floor.

sentences.zh: 葛王見殺宗敏，問於眾曰：「國王何罪而死？

translations.literal: The Prince of Ge, seeing Zong Min killed, asked the assembly: 「What crime had the Kingdom Prince that he should die?
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ge saw Zong Min slain and asked those present: 「What crime had the Kingdom Prince, that he should die?

sentences.zh: 」烏帶曰：「天許大事，尚已行之，此蟣虱耳，何足道者。

translations.literal: 」Wudai said: 「A Heaven-sanctioned great affair we have already carried through—this is a louse or nit; what is there worth speaking of?
translations.idiomatic: 」Wudai said: 「We have already done what Heaven approved—this is a flea. Why speak of it?

sentences.zh: 」天德三年，海陵追封宗敏為太師，進封爵。

translations.literal: 」In the third year of Tiande, Hailing posthumously enfeoffed Zong Min as Grand Preceptor and advanced his noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: 」In Tiande year 3 Hailing posthumously made Zong Min Grand Preceptor and raised his title of nobility.

sentences.zh: 妃蒲察氏，進國號。

translations.literal: His consort, of the Pucha clan, was advanced in state-title.
translations.idiomatic: His consort of the Pucha clan was raised in court rank.

sentences.zh: 封子撒合輦舒國公，賜名褒，進封王；

translations.literal: His son Sahelian was enfeoffed Duke of Shu, given the name Bao, and advanced to prince;
translations.idiomatic: His son Sahelian was made Duke of Shu, granted the name Bao, and later raised to prince;

sentences.zh: 阿里罕封密國公。

translations.literal: Alihan was enfeoffed Duke of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Alihan was enfeoffed Duke of Mi.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年，契丹撒八反，海陵遣使殺諸宗室，阿里罕遂見殺。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenglong the Khitan Saba rebelled; Hailing sent envoys to kill the members of the imperial clan, and Alihan was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglong year 6: the Khitan Saba rose in revolt. Hailing sent agents to slaughter the clan, and Alihan was killed.

sentences.zh: 大定間，詔複官爵。

translations.literal: In the Dading era an edict restored their offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dading an edict restored their offices and noble ranks.

sentences.zh: 胙王元，景宣皇帝峻子也，本名常勝，為北京留守，弟查刺為安武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Yuan, Prince of Zu, was a son of the Jingxuan Emperor Jun; his original name was Changsheng. He was Northern Capital regent; his younger brother Chaci was military commissioner of the Anwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, Prince of Zu, son of the Jingxuan Emperor Jun, was born Changsheng. He served as regent at the Northern Capital; his brother Chaci was military commissioner of the Anwu Army.

sentences.zh: 皇統七年四月戊午，左副點檢蒲察阿虎特子尚主，進禮物，賜宴便殿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huangtong, on the day wuwu of the fourth month, the son of Left Vice Director of the Palace Inspection Bureau Pucha Ahute married the princess and presented wedding gifts; a feast was granted in the Informal Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Huangtong year 7, fourth month, day wuwu: the son of Left Vice Director of the Palace Inspection Bureau Pucha Ahute married a princess and brought wedding gifts; the emperor gave a feast in the Informal Hall.

sentences.zh: 熙宗被酒，酌酒賜元，元不能飲，上怒，仗劍逼之，元逃去。

translations.literal: Xizong was drunk, poured wine and bestowed it on Yuan; Yuan could not drink—the sovereign grew angry, drew his sword and pressed him; Yuan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong, already drunk, poured wine and pressed it on Yuan. Yuan could not drink. The emperor flew into a rage, sword in hand, and drove at him; Yuan fled.

sentences.zh: 命左丞宗憲召元，宗憲與元俱去，上益怒，是時戶部尚書宗禮在側，使之跪，手殺之。

translations.literal: He ordered Left Vice Director Zongxian to summon Yuan; Zongxian went off with Yuan together—the sovereign grew still angrier. At that time Minister of Revenue Zongli was at his side; he made him kneel and killed him with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Left Vice Director Zongxian to fetch Yuan; Zongxian left with him, and the emperor’s wrath only mounted. Minister of Revenue Zongli stood nearby—the emperor forced him to his knees and killed him himself.

sentences.zh: 海陵與唐括辯謀廢立，海陵曰：「若舉大事，誰當立者。

translations.literal: Hailing and Tangguo Bian plotted deposition and enthronement; Hailing said: 「If we undertake a great affair, who ought to be enthroned?
translations.idiomatic: Hailing and Tangguo Bian plotted to depose the throne. Hailing asked: 「If we raise a coup, whom should we set up?

sentences.zh: 」海陵意謂己乃太祖長房之孫，當立。

translations.literal: 」Hailing’s intent was that he himself, as a grandson of the Taizu of the senior line, ought to be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hailing meant himself—grandson of Taizu in the senior house—to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 而辯與秉德初意不在海陵，常勝乃熙宗之弟，辯答曰：「無胙王常勝乎。

translations.literal: But Bian and Bingde at first had not had Hailing in mind; Changsheng was Xizong’s younger brother—Bian answered: 「Is there not the Prince of Zu, Changsheng?
translations.idiomatic: Bian and Bingde had not first thought of Hailing. Changsheng was Xizong’s own brother. Bian said: 「What of the Prince of Zu, Changsheng?

sentences.zh: 」海陵複問其次，辯曰：「鄧王子阿楞。

translations.literal: 」Hailing asked again who came next; Bian said: 「Prince of Deng’s son Aleng.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hailing pressed for the next choice. Bian said: 「Aleng, son of the Prince of Deng.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「阿楞屬疏。

translations.literal: 」Hailing said: 「Aleng’s line is remote.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hailing said: 「Aleng is too far from the line.

sentences.zh: 」由是海陵謂胙王有人望，不除之將不得立，故心忌常勝並阿楞。

translations.literal: 」From this Hailing judged that the Prince of Zu had the people’s regard—unless he were removed he could not be enthroned; therefore in his heart he envied Changsheng together with Aleng.
translations.idiomatic: 」Thence Hailing reckoned the Prince of Zu held the people’s favor—without removing him he could not reign—and so he hated Changsheng and Aleng alike.

sentences.zh: 是時，阿楞方為奉國上將軍。

translations.literal: At that time Aleng was serving as General-in-Chief Who Upholds the State.
translations.idiomatic: Aleng was then General-in-Chief Who Upholds the State.

sentences.zh: 河南軍士孫進自稱「皇弟按察大王」，熙宗疑「皇弟」二字或在常勝也，使特思鞫之，無狀。

translations.literal: A soldier of the Henan army, Sun Jin, styled himself 「Younger Brother, Inspector King」; Xizong suspected the words 「younger brother」 might point to Changsheng, and had Tesi interrogate him—no proof emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jin, a soldier in Henan, called himself 「Younger Brother, Inspector King.」 Xizong wondered whether 「younger brother」 meant Changsheng and set Tesi to question him; nothing was proved.

sentences.zh: 特思乃嘗疑海陵與唐括辯時時竊議，告之悼後者。

translations.literal: Tesi had once suspected that Hailing and Tangguo Bian from time to time met in secret counsel, and reported this to Empress Dowager Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Tesi had long suspected Hailing and Tangguo Bian of meeting in secret, and had told Empress Dowager Dao.

sentences.zh: 海陵知熙宗有疑常勝心，因此可以除之，謂熙宗曰：「孫進反有端，不稱他人，乃稱皇弟大王。

translations.literal: Hailing knew Xizong already doubted Changsheng, and that by this he could remove him; he said to Xizong: 「Sun Jin’s rebellion has a basis—he named no other man, only Younger Brother the King.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing saw that Xizong already doubted Changsheng and that here was his chance. He told Xizong: 「Sun Jin’s revolt has a thread to pull—he named no one else but Younger Brother the King.

sentences.zh: 陛下弟止有常勝、查刺。

translations.literal: Your Majesty’s brothers are only Changsheng and Chaci.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only two brothers—Changsheng and Chaci.

sentences.zh: 特思鞫不以實，故出之矣。

translations.literal: Tesi’s interrogation did not bring out the truth, and so he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Tesi’s inquiry did not get at the truth, and so he was let go.

sentences.zh: 」熙宗以為然，使唐括辯、蕭肄按問特思，特思自誣服，故出常勝罪。

translations.literal: 」Xizong thought it so, and had Tangguo Bian and Xiao Yi examine and question Tesi; Tesi falsely confessed, and thus the charge against Changsheng was established.
translations.idiomatic: 」Xizong agreed and set Tangguo Bian and Xiao Yi to press Tesi; Tesi confessed under torture, and Changsheng was condemned.

sentences.zh: 於是，乃殺常勝及其弟查刺，並殺特思。

translations.literal: Thereupon they killed Changsheng and his brother Chaci, and killed Tesi as well.
translations.idiomatic: Then they killed Changsheng and his brother Chaci, and killed Tesi too.

sentences.zh: 海陵乘此並擠阿楞殺之。

translations.literal: Hailing seized the moment and, pressing the case, had Aleng killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing used the moment to force Aleng’s death as well.

sentences.zh: 阿楞弟撻楞，熙宗本無意殺之，海陵曰：「其兄既已伏誅，其弟安得獨存。

translations.literal: Aleng’s younger brother Taleng—Xizong at first had no mind to kill him; Hailing said: 「His elder brother has already suffered execution—how can the younger brother alone remain?
translations.idiomatic: Aleng’s brother Taleng—Xizong had not meant to kill him. Hailing said: 「The elder brother is already dead—can the younger live alone?

sentences.zh: 」又殺之。

translations.literal: 」They killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: 」They killed him as well.

sentences.zh: 熙宗以海陵為忠，愈益任之，而不知其詐也。

translations.literal: Xizong took Hailing for loyal and trusted him all the more, not knowing his deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong thought Hailing faithful and relied on him ever more heavily, never seeing the fraud.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，追封常勝、查刺、阿楞官爵，親臨葬所致祭。

translations.literal: When Hailing usurped the throne he posthumously restored the offices and titles of Changsheng, Chaci, and Aleng, and in person came to their burials to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hailing seized the throne he posthumously restored Changsheng, Chaci, and Aleng, and came in person to their graves to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 大定十三年六月丁巳，世宗召皇太子諸王，侍食於清輝殿，曰：「或稱海陵多能，何也。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dading, on the day dingsi of the sixth month, Shizong summoned the crown prince and the princes to attend him at meal in the Clear Splendor Hall, and said: 「Some call Hailing greatly capable—why?
translations.idiomatic: Dading year 13, sixth month, day dingsi: Shizong called the crown prince and the princes to dine with him in the Clear Splendor Hall and said: 「Some praise Hailing as a man of many talents—why?

sentences.zh: 海陵譎詐，睢盱殺人，空虛天下三分之二。

translations.literal: Hailing was treacherous and false, glaring and killing men, and emptied two-thirds of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was sly and murderous; he glared down the court and killed until a third of the realm stood empty.

sentences.zh: 太祖諸孫中，惟胙王元天性賢者也。」

translations.literal: Among the Taizu’s grandsons, only Prince of Zu Yuan was gifted with a worthy nature by Heaven.」
translations.idiomatic: Of Taizu’s grandsons, only Prince of Zu Yuan was truly worthy by nature.」

sentences.zh: 元子育，本名合住，大定二十七年，自南京副留守遷大宗正丞，兼勸農副使。

translations.literal: Yuan’s son Yu, original name Hezhu—in the twenty-seventh year of Dading he moved from deputy regent of the Southern Capital to Grand Director of the Imperial Clan, and concurrently Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan’s son Yu, born Hezhu: in Dading year 27 he went from deputy regent at the Southern Capital to Grand Director of the Imperial Clan and Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 上問宰臣曰：「合住為人如何？

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers: 「What sort of man is Hezhu?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his chief ministers: 「What manner of man is Hezhu?

sentences.zh: 」平章政事襄、參政宗浩對曰：「為人清廉幹治。

translations.literal: 」Grand Councilor Xiang and Vice Councilor Zonghao replied: 「In conduct he is clean, honest, and capable in administration.
translations.idiomatic: 」Grand Councilor Xiang and Vice Councilor Zonghao answered: 「Upright, frugal, and able in office.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「乃父亦然。

translations.literal: 」The emperor said: 「His father was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor said: 「His father was the same.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「蒲陽溫胙王元，外若愚訥，臨事明敏過人。

translations.literal: 」He added: 「Puyangwen, Prince of Zu Yuan—outwardly dull and slow of speech, yet in affairs keener than other men.
translations.idiomatic: 」He went on: 「Puyangwen—Prince of Zu Yuan—seemed slow and tongue-tied, yet in business he outshone everyone.

sentences.zh: 朕于兄弟間，于元尤款密。」

translations.literal: Among my brothers, toward Yuan I was especially close and intimate.」
translations.idiomatic: Of all my brothers, none was dearer to me than Yuan.」

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「太祖躬擐甲胄，以定國家，舉無遺策，而諸子勇略材識，足以遂父之志。

translations.literal: The encomium says: 「The Taizu himself donned armor to settle the state; in every move nothing was left to chance—and his sons’ courage, strategy, talent, and judgment were enough to fulfill their father’s design.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: 「Taizu took the field in armor to found the realm and never left a move to chance. His sons had courage, plan, and wit enough to finish what he began.

sentences.zh: 傳及太宗，而諸孫享其成矣。

translations.literal: The line passed to Taizong, and the grandsons reaped what was already won.」
translations.idiomatic: It reached Taizong, and the grandsons lived on the harvest.」
